method: Binary floors read from the Microsoft runtime archives (dotnet-runtime / windowsdesktop-runtime zip and tar.gz): first and last release of every major per os/arch, bisected to the exact release wherever the floor changed. Windows: EXE subsystem version plus static imports of the core runtime files (dotnet.exe, hostfxr, hostpolicy, coreclr, clrjit, System.*.Native) checked against the Windows version that introduced each function (ReactOS export tables with -version tags, corrected from Microsoft Learn 'Minimum supported client'); for the Windows Desktop runtime all of its own DLLs count. Delay-loaded imports (WinRT API sets) and optional libraries (msquic.dll, QUIC only) are reported in evidence but do not set min_os. UCRT: 2.0-6.0 ship the Universal CRT app-locally, 1.x and 7.0+ need the system UCRT (built into Windows 10, KB2999226 before). macOS: highest LC_BUILD_VERSION minos of any Mach-O. Linux: highest GLIBC_x.y symbol version of any ELF. Rules for the runtime also cover the ASP.NET Core runtime, the SDK and the Windows Desktop runtime of the same release (releases.json gives all of them the runtime's version number); the Windows Desktop runtime has additional rules of its own and both must pass. .NET Framework rules come from Microsoft's version/OS tables (no binary check: the offline installers enforce their own OS blocks).
filters: Rules narrow the files they cover with variant / kind / format (SCHEMA.md) and, where only the file name tells builds apart, file_match: a regex on the download file name (1.x per-distro Linux builds, the 2.1-3.1 rhel.6-x64 builds, the portable linux-x64/arm64/arm builds). variant null = the .NET Framework installers. Framework rules add built_in: the Windows ids that ship that Framework version preinstalled (or as an optional feature, see notes).
musl: linux-musl (Alpine) archives are not covered: os_versions.json has no musl ids.
